{"sql": "SELECT 
    t.pickup_date,
    t.pickup_dow,
    COUNT(*) AS trips_in_window,
    COUNT(DISTINCT t.pickup_hour) AS hours_in_window,
    COUNT(*)::FLOAT / COUNT(DISTINCT t.pickup_hour) AS trips_per_hour
FROM investigator.trips t
WHERE

{"sql": "SELECT w.day,
       w.precip_mm,
       w.wmo_code,
       COUNT(t.trip_id) AS trips_in_window
FROM investigator.nyc_daily_weather w
LEFT JOIN investigator.trips t
  ON t.pickup_date = w.day
 AND t.is_valid_trip
 AND t.pickup_hour BETWEEN 12 AND 23
WHERE w.day IN ('2024-07-27','2024-07-31')
GROUP BY w.day, w.precip_mm, w.wmo_code
ORDER BY w.day", "why": "This query applies the like-for-like window (pickup_hour BETWEEN 12 AND 23) to both focus days, ensuring a fair comparison of trip counts within the shared 12-hour period. By filtering to the same hour range on both Saturday and Wednesday, we eliminate the coverage bias where Saturday has only 13 hours of data versus Wednesday's full 24 hours. The LEFT JOIN preserves both days in the output even if one has zero trips, and GROUP BY day/precip/wmo_code isolates whether weather conditions differ between the two days while holding the time window constant. This directly tests Hypothesis H2: if Saturday shows significantly fewer trips than Wednesday within the identical 12–23 window, weather is a likely suppressor of demand. The results will show the observed precipitation and WMO weather code for each day alongside the associated trip counts, allowing an assessment of whether the weather conditions on Saturday 2024-07-27 (e.g., higher precipitation) coincided with the lower trip count of 59,736 compared to Wednesday 2024-07-31's 70,674."}

ca73bc3638ba9d3dc61d2675.text:
{
  "sql": "SELECT t.pickup_date,
       t.pickup_dow,
       COUNT(*) AS trips_in_window,
       COUNT(DISTINCT t.pickup_hour) AS hours_in_window,
       COUNT(*)::FLOAT / COUNT(DISTINCT t.pickup_hour) AS trips_per_hour
FROM investigator.trips t
WHERE t.pickup_date IN ('2024-07-31','2024-08-01')
  AND t.pickup_hour BETWEEN 0 AND 13
  AND t.is_valid_trip
GROUP BY t.pickup_date, t.pickup_dow",
  "why": "This query computes the hourly trip rate (trips per hour) for Thursday and Wednesday within the like-for-like 0–13 window. By dividing total trips by the count of distinct hours that actually have data (14 for both days, since the window is fixed to 0–13), we normalize for the shared coverage. The results directly test H4: if the trips_per_hour ratio is close to 1.0, the 2.2% raw trip count difference (39,778 vs 38,972) is due to random variation within the shared hours; if it deviates significantly, it indicates intrinsic demand differences persisting after fair hourly normalization."
}

{"sql": "SELECT 
    w.day,
    w.precip_mm,
    w.rain_mm,
    w.wmo_code,
    COUNT(t.trip_id) AS valid_trips,
    COUNT(DISTINCT t.pickup_hour) AS hours_covered,
    ROUND(COUNT(t.trip_id)/NULLIF(COUNT(DISTINCT t.pickup_hour),0),2) AS trips_per_hour
FROM investigator.nyc_daily_weather w
LEFT JOIN investigator.trips t
  ON t.pickup_date = w.day
 AND t.is_valid_trip
WHERE w.day IN ('2024-07-30','2024-07-31')
GROUP BY w.day, w.precip_mm, w.rain_mm, w.wmo_code
ORDER BY w.day", "why": "This query tests H1 by comparing total valid taxi trips and the normalized trips-per-hour metric between the rainy Wednesday (2024-07-31) and dry Tuesday (2024-07-30). By including precip_mm, rain_mm, and wmo_code, the weather conditions are explicitly captured. The trips_per_hour metric normalizes total trips by the number of distinct hours covered, allowing assessment of whether rain reduced demand after accounting for data coverage differences. GROUP BY isolates the weather-day effect, and ORDER BY ensures a clear side-by-side view. The LEFT JOIN guarantees both days appear even if one lacks trip data."}

    COUNT(*) AS total_valid_trips,
    COUNT(DISTINCT t.pickup_hour) AS hours_covered,
    ROUND(COUNT(*)/NULLIF(COUNT(DISTINCT t.pickup_hour),0),1) AS trips_per_hour,
    SUM(CASE WHEN t.pickup_zone IN ('JFK Airport','LaGuardia Airport','Newark Airport')
                OR t.dropoff_zone IN ('JFK Airport','LaGuardia Airport','Newark Airport')
                THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS airport_trips,
    ROUND(1.0 * SUM(CASE WHEN t.pickup_zone IN ('JFK Airport','LaGuardia Airport','Newark Airport')
                OR t.dropoff_zone IN ('JFK Airport','LaGuardia Airport','Newark Airport')
                THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)
         / NULLIF(COUNT(DISTINCT t.pickup_hour),0),1) AS airport_trips_per_hour,
       AVG(w.temp_max_c) AS avg_temp_max,
       AVG(w.precip_mm) AS avg_precip_mm
FROM investigator.trips t
LEFT JOIN investigator.nyc_daily_weather w ON t.pickup_date = w.day
WHERE t.pickup_date IN ('2024-07-30','2024-07-31')
  AND t.is_valid_trip
GROUP BY t.pickup_date

    t.pickup_date,
    t.pickup_hour,
    COUNT(*) AS valid_trips,
    COUNT(DISTINCT t.pickup_ts) AS hours_covered,
    ROUND(COUNT(*)/NULLIF(COUNT(DISTINCT t.pickup_ts),0),2) AS trips_per_hour,
    SUM(CASE WHEN t.pickup_zone IN ('JFK Airport','LaGuardia Airport','Newark Airport')
                OR t.dropoff_zone IN ('JFK Airport','LaGuardia Airport','Newark Airport')
                THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS airport_trips,
    ROUND(1.0 * SUM(CASE WHEN t.pickup_zone IN ('JFK Airport','LaGuardia Airport','Newark Airport')
                OR t.dropoff_zone IN ('JFK Airport','LaGuardia Airport','Newark Airport')
                THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)
         / NULLIF(COUNT(DISTINCT t.pickup_ts),0),2) AS airport_trips_per_hour,
    AVG(w.precip_mm) AS avg_precip_mm,
    AVG(w.wmo_code) AS avg_wmo_code
FROM investigator.trips t
LEFT JOIN investigator.nyc_daily_weather w
  ON t.pickup_date = w.day
WHERE t.is_valid_trip
  AND t.pickup_date IN ('2024-07-30','2024-07-31')
GROUP BY t.pickup_date, t.pickup_hour
ORDER BY t.pickup_date, t.pickup_hour", "why": "This query tests H4 by breaking demand into hour-level buckets for each comparison day. Grouping by both pickup_date and pickup_hour allows a fair hour-by-hour comparison between the rainy Wednesday (2024-07-31) and dry Tuesday (2024-07-30), satisfying the rule that demand varies by hour. Including weather columns (avg_precip_mm, avg_wmo_code) confirms the rain presence on 2024-07-31 and allows inspection of whether the hour-by-hour demand drop is consistent with precipitation. Airport trip shares are also tracked per hour to see if rain specifically suppressed airport trips during certain periods, addressing the day-of-week confounding by showing the granular weather-demand relationship."}

json.focus: 2024-08-01 (Thursday, partial 14h coverage 00:00–13:59) vs 2024-07-31 (Wednesday, full 24h coverage), using the profiler's like-for-like window of pickup_hour BETWEEN 0 AND 13
json.baseline: Wednesday 2024-07-31 full-day baseline (38,972 trips in the 0–13 window); compare Thursday 2024-08-01 trips in the same window (39,778) to the Wednesday baseline

hypotheses.claim: Thursday 2024-08-01 has intrinsically lower trip rates than Wednesday 2024-07-31 even within shared hours (0–13), due to day-of-week patterns (e.g., reduced commuter travel, different leisure timing on Thursdays vs Wednesdays).

hypotheses.claim: Weather on Thursday 2024-08-01 (e.g., higher precipitation, extreme heat, or severe storms) suppressed demand relative to the fair weather on Wednesday 2024-07-31.

hypotheses.claim: Airport-related trips were disproportionately low on Thursday 2024-08-01 compared to Wednesday 2024-07-31, dragging down the total within the 0–13 window.

reviews.reason: The query correctly isolates the 0–13 window for both days, yielding 14 hours on each. The result rows show Thursday: 39,778 trips; Wednesday: 38,972 trips. The finding accurately restates these totals and notes the identical window width, correctly observing that totals alone cannot isolate per-hour rates. No invented numbers or over-generalised claims about other days.

The query result shows Thursday had 0.1 mm rain / wmo_code 51 and Wednesday had 9.9 mm rain / wmo_code 63. The analyst's finding states Thursday had 'extreme heat' (wmo_code 51) and implies suppressed demand relative to fair weather on Wednesday. However, wmo_code 51 is typically 'mist' or 'fog' in the NOAA schema, not extreme heat, and the finding mislabels the weather condition. More importantly, the finding claims the drop 'suggests extreme heat suppressed trips rather than rain' but the data shows Thursday had FEWER hours in the original 24h day but MORE trips in the 0–13 window compared to Wednesday, and the weather labels are inaccurate. The evidence does not support attributing any demand change to extreme heat; it only shows a correlation between the observed conditions and trip counts for these two days within the shared window. The finding over-interprets the weather's role and uses an incorrect weather label.
reviews.revision_request: Restate the finding to describe the observed weather conditions on each day (precip amounts and wmo_codes) and the associated trip counts within the 0–13 window. Do not claim that extreme heat suppressed demand or that weather definitively caused the difference; the data is consistent with either role and the weather labels are inaccurate.

reviews.reason: The query correctly computes total and airport trips within the 0–13 window for both days. The result rows show Thursday: 39,778 total / 4,415 airport (11.1%); Wednesday: 38,972 total / 4,213 airport (10.8%). The finding accurately notes the slightly higher proportion on Thursday and that absolute airport trip counts are higher on Thursday, which is a correct interpretation of the data. No invented numbers or over-generalised claims.

missing_hypothesis.claim: Compare the hourly trip rate (trips per hour) within the 0–13 window for Thursday vs Wednesday to determine if the 2.2% gap (39,778 vs 38,972) persists when normalized by the 13 shared hours, which would indicate whether the difference is due to within-hour demand variation or other factors.
missing_hypothesis.test: SELECT t.pickup_date, COUNT(*)::FLOAT / COUNT(DISTINCT t.pickup_hour) AS trips_per_hour FROM investigator.trips t WHERE t.pickup_date IN ('2024-07-31','2024-08-01') AND t.pickup_hour BETWEEN 0 AND 13 AND t.is_valid_trip GROUP BY t.pickup_date;

data_caveats: The 0–13 window excludes the evening/night hours (14–23). Thursday's coverage ends at 13:59, while Wednesday has full 24h coverage. The profiler explicitly warns against dividing totals by hours covered because the missing hours are quiet night/morning hours, so that inflates the partial day—but here the window is fixed 0–13 for both, so the comparison of trips_in_window is valid within that constraint.
Airport trip percentages are similar (~11%) on both days, suggesting airport effects are proportional rather than a disproportionate driver of the gap.

  "sql": "SELECT t.pickup_date,
       t.pickup_dow,
       COUNT(*) AS trips_in_window,
       COUNT(DISTINCT t.pickup_hour) AS hours_in_window,
       COUNT(*)::FLOAT / COUNT(DISTINCT t.pickup_hour) AS trips_per_hour
FROM investigator.trips t
WHERE t.pickup_date IN ('2024-07-31','2024-08-01')
  AND t.pickup_hour BETWEEN 0 AND 13
  AND t.is_valid_trip
GROUP BY t.pickup_date, t.pickup_dow",
  "why": "This query computes the hourly trip rate (trips per hour) for Thursday and Wednesday within the like-for-like 0–13 window. By dividing total trips by the count of distinct hours that actually have data (14 for both days, since the window is fixed to 0–13), we normalize for the shared coverage. The results directly test H4: if the trips_per_hour ratio is close to 1.0, the 2.2% raw trip count difference (39,778 vs 38,972) is due to random variation within the shared hours; if it deviates significantly, it indicates intrinsic demand differences persisting after fair hourly normalization."
}

json.answer: Within the 12–23 hour window, Wednesday 2024-07-31 had 70,674 trips versus Saturday 2024-07-27's 59,736, a 15.5% like-for-like gap after accounting for the 12 shared hours. H1 confirms that even in this shared window, Wednesday consistently outperforms Saturday, indicating intrinsic weekday demand patterns (commuter/business travel) outweigh weekend leisure patterns. H3 further shows that airport trips were proportionally similar (~10%) but absolutely lower on Saturday (6,082 vs 6,900), contributing to the total shortfall but not driving it disproportionately. The raw whole-day gap of -39.2% is partly a data-coverage artefact (missing early morning/late night hours), but a real 15.5% difference persists when comparing the same 12-hour window.

hypotheses.claim: Rain on 2024-07-31 shifted trip destinations away from airports and toward nearer zones, reducing airport‑trip share relative to the dry Tuesday.

hypotheses.claim: Rain on 2024-07-31 changed the geographic distribution of trips across boroughs/zones (e.g., fewer trips to Manhattan, more intra-borough), detectable via zone-level volume shifts.

{"sql": "SELECT 
    t.pickup_date,
    COUNT(*) AS total_valid_trips,
    COUNT(DISTINCT t.pickup_hour) AS hours_covered,
    ROUND(COUNT(*)/NULLIF(COUNT(DISTINCT t.pickup_hour),0),1) AS trips_per_hour,
    SUM(CASE WHEN t.pickup_zone IN ('JFK Airport','LaGuardia Airport','Newark Airport')
                OR t.dropoff_zone IN ('JFK Airport','LaGuardia Airport','Newark Airport')
                THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS airport_trips,
    ROUND(1.0 * SUM(CASE WHEN t.pickup_zone IN ('JFK Airport','LaGuardia Airport','Newark Airport')
                OR t.dropoff_zone IN ('JFK Airport','LaGuardia Airport','Newark Airport')
                THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)
         / NULLIF(COUNT(DISTINCT t.pickup_hour),0),1) AS airport_trips_per_hour,
       AVG(w.temp_max_c) AS avg_temp_max,
       AVG(w.precip_mm) AS avg_precip_mm
FROM investigator.trips t
LEFT JOIN investigator.nyc_daily_weather w ON t.pickup_date = w.day
WHERE t.pickup_date IN ('2024-07-30','2024-07-31')
  AND t.is_valid_trip
GROUP BY t.pickup_date", "why": "This query tests H2 by comparing rainy Wednesday 2024-07-31 against dry Tuesday 2024-07-30. {"sql": "SELECT 
    t.pickup_date,
    t.pickup_hour,
    COUNT(*) AS valid_trips,
    COUNT(DISTINCT t.pickup_ts) AS hours_covered,
    ROUND(COUNT(*)/NULLIF(COUNT(DISTINCT t.pickup_ts),0),2) AS trips_per_hour,
    SUM(CASE WHEN t.pickup_zone IN ('JFK Airport','LaGuardia Airport','Newark Airport')
                OR t.dropoff_zone IN ('JFK Airport','LaGuardia Airport','Newark Airport')
                THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS airport_trips,
    ROUND(1.0 * SUM(CASE WHEN t.pickup_zone IN ('JFK Airport','LaGuardia Airport','Newark Airport')
                OR t.dropoff_zone IN ('JFK Airport','LaGuardia Airport','Newark Airport')
                THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)
         / NULLIF(COUNT(DISTINCT t.pickup_ts),0),2) AS airport_trips_per_hour,
    AVG(w.precip_mm) AS avg_precip_mm,
    AVG(w.wmo_code) AS avg_wmo_code
FROM investigator.trips t
LEFT JOIN investigator.nyc_daily_weather w
  ON t.pickup_date = w.day
WHERE t.is_valid_trip
  AND t.pickup_date IN ('2024-07-30','2024-07-31')
GROUP BY t.pickup_date, t.pickup_hour
ORDER BY t.pickup_date, t.pickup_hour", "why": "This query tests H4 by breaking demand into hour-level buckets for each comparison day. Grouping by both pickup_date and pickup_hour allows a fair hour-by-hour comparison between the rainy Wednesday (2024-07-31) and dry Tuesday (2024-07-30), satisfying the rule that demand varies by hour. Including weather columns (avg_precip_mm, avg_wmo_code) confirms the rain presence on 2024-07-31 and allows inspection of whether the hour-by-hour demand drop is consistent with precipitation. Airport trip shares are also tracked per hour to see if rain specifically suppressed airport trips during certain periods, addressing the day-of-week confounding by showing the granular weather-demand relationship."}

{"sql": "SELECT 
    t.pickup_date,
    t.pickup_hour,
    COUNT(*) AS valid_trips,
    COUNT(DISTINCT t.pickup_ts) AS hours_covered,
    ROUND(COUNT(*)/NULLIF(COUNT(DISTINCT t.pickup_ts),0),2) AS trips_per_hour,
    SUM(CASE WHEN t.pickup_zone IN ('JFK Airport','LaGuardia Airport','Newark Airport')
                OR t.dropoff_zone IN ('JFK Airport','LaGuardia Airport','Newark Airport')
                THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS airport_trips,
    ROUND(1.0 * SUM(CASE WHEN t.pickup_zone IN ('JFK Airport','LaGuardia Airport','Newark Airport')
                OR t.dropoff_zone IN ('JFK Airport','LaGuardia Airport','Newark Airport')
                THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)
         / NULLIF(COUNT(DISTINCT t.pickup_ts),0),2) AS airport_trips_per_hour,
    AVG(w.precip_mm) AS avg_precip_mm,
    AVG(w.wmo_code) AS avg_wmo_code
FROM investigator.trips t
LEFT JOIN investigator.nyc_daily_weather w
  ON t.pickup_date = w.day
WHERE t.is_valid_trip
  AND t.pickup_date IN ('2024-07-30','2024-07-31')
GROUP BY t.pickup_date, t.pickup_hour
ORDER BY t.pickup_date, t.pickup_hour", "why": "This query tests H4 by breaking demand into hour-level buckets for each comparison day. Grouping by both pickup_date and pickup_hour allows a fair hour-by-hour comparison between the rainy Wednesday (2024-07-31) and dry Tuesday (2024-07-30), satisfying the rule that demand varies by hour. Including weather columns (avg_precip_mm, avg_wmo_code) confirms the rain presence on 2024-07-31 and allows inspection of whether the hour-by-hour demand drop is consistent with precipitation. Airport trip shares are also tracked per hour to see if rain specifically suppressed airport trips during certain periods, addressing the day-of-week confounding by showing the granular weather-demand relationship."}
